Single–particle energy levels in a 1-D infinite well are  

εₙ = n² E , n = 1,2,3,… , E = π²ħ² /(2mL²).

Because the particles are identical spin-½ fermions, each spatial level can hold at most two particles (spin up and spin down).

Ground state (fill the lowest available levels):
• n = 1 : 2 particles  energy 2·1²E = 2E  
• n = 2 : 2 particles  energy 2·2²E = 2·4E = 8E  
Total ground-state energy: 2E + 8E = 10E.

First excited state (make the smallest possible single excitation):
Move one particle from n = 2 to the next empty level n = 3.
Occupancy: n = 1 (2), n = 2 (1), n = 3 (1).  
Energy: 2·1²E + 1·2²E + 1·3²E = 2E + 4E + 9E = 15E.

Second excited state (next larger total energy):
Keep n = 1 full, move one particle from n = 1 up to n = 3.
Occupancy: n = 1 (1), n = 2 (2), n = 3 (1).  
Energy: 1·1²E + 2·2²E + 1·3²E = 1E + 8E + 9E = 18E.

(The other obvious possibility—placing both particles in n = 3—gives 20E, which is higher, so 18E is indeed the second excited level.)

Thus

Ground state energy   = 10E  
First excited energy  = 15E  
Second excited energy = 18E

Comparing with the offered choices, only option (D) matches.

Answer: D
